name: BSP_Game_SyncLobbySettingsFromLua
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __fastcall void(void), body 005e2f00..005e3282, sole caller 004dfb70 BSP_Game_LoadMissionScene. Opens the Lua global table named by 00cf1f28 ("LobbySettings") through BSP_LuaStateOwner_GetGlobals/BSP_LuaObject_*, then walks the 14-slot pointer array at 00e08908 (slot 0Dh is the null at 00e08940, which is why the loop at 005e2f6f skips index 0Dh by number). The 13 field names are PlayerCount, Map, GameMode, MapSize, UnitType, ResourceLimit, TimeLimit, TimeLimit_IC, PointLimit, RoundLimit, EnablePowerups, EnableMap, ReloadPayload. 005e2f8b excludes slots 0 and 2 from the read-back branch. Also sets DAT_00e0c978/DAT_00e17bf2/DAT_00e08880 from DAT_00e19584/8c/88 and the effective game mode via 004bca50. Installed-file-checked: the multiplayer mission scripts under Scripts/missions/multi read exactly eight of these thirteen names and no others; creating the table with these names makes four previously failing duel scripts run clean in bsp_mission_script_probe. docs/MISSION_LUA_MACHINE.md | Run-time evidence, packet cc_exe_2f: reached at its only call site 004e02d0 inside 004dfb70. The executable creates the LobbySettings global with the thirteen recovered field names so a script can index it, and records the routine as unimplemented because every value it syncs comes from session state this process does not own. Note that bsp/mission_scene_load.hpp still calls this host method lua_reset_state, which is a call-site guess: the body resets no Lua state. | Values established. The fourteen ints at 00e1955c are stored option indices, one per name slot, written by 005d49e0 and 005d6350 and replicated into the network state record by 0076c2c0. Per slot the Lua type comes from the option registry 00576b10: a non-zero integer payload at (slot, 0) means the slot publishes a number (005e31a0), zero means it publishes the label 005e2320 builds (005e31d4). Only slot 5 ResourceLimit has integer option keys in Scripts/datatables/MultiGlobals.lua MultiLobbySettings, so twelve of the thirteen fields are strings. A slot whose 005d5500 menu row is -1 and which is neither 0 nor 2 is written nil. The gate at 005e2f99 leaves the global nil in single player (no session and not forced) after the 005e2f59 clear; 005e2fce writes the effective mode into slot 2 and, below mode 4, into slot 3, because modes 0..3 are the four Island Capture map sizes. Flags: 00e0c978 = EnablePowerups is option 0, 00e17bf2 = ReloadPayload is option 0, 00e08880 = EnableMap is option 0, forced to 1,0,1 in single player. 00e0cfb4 takes twice the ResourceLimit payload below mode 4, else 2400.0f from 00ce396c. docs/MISSION_LOBBY_SETTINGS.md; include/bsp/mission_lobby_settings.hpp. | Run-time evidence, packet cc_exe_2j (bsp_game.exe milestone 2j): the reconstruction runs in bsp_game.exe at the load's 004E02D0 row, replacing milestone 2f's invented substitute (a zeroed thirteen-field LobbySettings table, created on the reasoning that a script would otherwise index a nil global). The routine's own answer is the opposite: game+1FE4h is zero in this single-player run, so the early-out at 005E2F93..005E2FCC sets the global nil at 005E2F59 and publishes no table. The USN02 mission Lua then reaches the same three bindings with no chunk error, so nothing in that mission indexed the global the substitute existed for. The mode flags come out (1, 0, 1) from the single-player branch at 005E2FAB and the command points as the 2400.0 at 00CE396C. The MultiLobbySettings option registry 008D2F50 and the label builder 005E2320 are host records; neither is reached on this path. docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2j.
